newsitem.title: ITALY: Genoa sets water/gas utility float offer price.
newsitem.headline: Genoa sets water/gas utility float offer price.

text.p: The Italian city of Genoa said it has set a public offer price of 1,300 lire per share for the flotation of its AMGA SpA water and gas utility to take place on October 7 and 8.
The public sale is of 151 million ordinary shares, equal to about 49 percent of the utility owned by the city.

Milan merchant bank Mediobanca, global coordinator for AMGA's privatisation, said in a statement the global offer comprised a public offer for a minimum of 60 million shares and a placement aimed at Italian and foreign institutional investors.
AMGA, which became the first Italian municipal utility to become a Societa per Azione, or joint stock company, last December, will be listed on the Milan stock exchange by the end of the year.
